subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Johnson <elise@finlytics.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Hi Elise 

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the performance items you flagged (TTFT + streaming cadence):

Summary of what I heard you say:
- Target Time-to-First-Token (TTFT): <= 150ms p95 for single-turn short responses (<= 64 tokens).
- Streaming delivery: SSE preferred for your web clients; fallback to WebSocket for mobile offline sync.
- Chunk cadence: small chunks every ~80-120ms for perceived responsiveness; larger chunk option for long-form streaming.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 250 req/s with burst to 1,000 req/s; expected sustained concurrency ~60 active streams.
- Fallbacks: plan to failover to a lower-cost model if latency spikes; you want <1% degraded-mode calls during peak.

Attachments: I attached a simple SLO matrix template (finlytics_slo_matrix.xlsx) so you can confirm the exact targets and scenarios.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the hard TTFT target and chunk cadence preferences in the matrix (Mark can fill technical constraints).
2) We run a short benchmark with our Sales Engineer to validate TTFT on a representative prompt set (we can scope token lengths and concurrency).
3) Sync: schedule a 45-min benchmark & architecture session next week (SE + SRE + your infra lead).

Pls let me know if the bullets above match your expectations and if the attached matrix covers the scenarios. I’ll loop in Dylan (SE) and Priyom (sales lead) to scope the load test once you confirm.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Elise Johnson <elise@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and yes that summary is accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- TTFT: firm requirement is p95 <= 150ms for short responses (up to 64 tokens). For long responses (>512 tokens) we can accept initial token at p95 <= 400ms if chunking starts within 200ms.
- Streaming: SSE is our default for web clients. For mobile we prefer WebSocket for better resume behavior. We want chunk cadence around 80-100ms for short answers; for long responses the cadence can move to ~200ms when bandwidth-constrained.
- Throughput/concurrency: projected steady state 200-300 req/s across our EU+US regions; peak bursts up to ~1k req/s during market open. Concurrent active streams estimate: 40-75 depending on release.
- Token budget: average completion length ~120 tokens, but worst-case up to 2,000 tokens for full reports.
- Observability: we need per-request TTFT metrics, chunk cadence logs, and a way to map degraded-mode invocations back to request ids.

We attached Mark's initial notes on infra constraints (he'll provide a short doc). We'll fill your SLO matrix and return by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Elise
Head of Product | FinLytics
elise@finlytics.com

Cc: Elise Johnson <elise@finlytics.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Dylan / Priyom — looping you both in. Elise confirmed the TTFT p95 <=150ms requirement for short answers and provided additional constraints (see quoted reply). Key ask: can SE scope a lightweight benchmark to validate TTFT + streaming cadence over SSE and WebSocket with the following test parameters?

Proposed benchmark scope (initial):
- Prompt set: 100 short prompts (<=64 tokens) and 20 long prompts (512-2,000 tokens) — representative of FinLytics top queries.
- Concurrency: run at 25 / 50 / 75 concurrent streams to observe TTFT and per-chunk cadence.
- Throughput ramp: steady-state 250 req/s then burst to 1,000 req/s for 5 minutes.
- Network emulation: simulate average mobile latency of 60ms and a bandwidth-constrained profile for long responses.
- Observability: capture per-request TTFT, chunk timestamps, and any degraded-mode fallbacks.

Please confirm if that scope is feasible and what infra (model variant, quantization, region) you want to use. Attach benchmark_plan.md with proposed test commands + data schema.

Also propose we schedule the architecture/benchmark call Wed 2026-04-14 10:00 AM PT (or Thu 11:00 AM PT). Elise — pls confirm availability.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: TTFT & streaming SLOs - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — scope looks good. Quick notes from SE perspective:

- Feasible: we can validate p95 TTFT <=150ms on our dedicated GPU pool for short prompts using a distilled open model + int8 quantization, running in us-west region.
- Streaming: SSE will be tested first (browser cadence instrumentation). We’ll also test WebSocket resume behavior for mobile.
- Chunk cadence: we’ll measure actual inter-chunk deltas. Expect some variance; if we can consistently hit ~80-120ms at low concurrency we’ll tune batching thresholds to keep that cadence.
- Throughput/concurrency: plan to run the 250 steady-state test on a 4x-GPU node set and burst test by spinning up one additional node group to emulate production autoscale.
- Observability: I’ll instrument request IDs + per-chunk telemetry and push logs to a shared S3 with a small manifest for FinLytics to ingest.

I’ll prepare a test runbook and kick off a dry run tomorrow morning. Proposed call: Wed 2026-04-14 10:00 AM PT works for me. Elise / Mark — can you confirm?

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
